opex.heading: Consolidated Operating Expenses
opex.text:
Depreciation and amortization charges relate to the depreciation of buildings and equipment related improvements, leasehold improvements, material handling equipment, furniture, fixtures, and our computer equipment. Amortization relates primarily to intangible assets for customer relationships.

Selling, general, and administrative expenses consist primarily of warehouse and non-warehouse related labor, administrative expenses, employee related costs, professional fees, equipment expenses, facility and warehouse costs, and information technology (including amortization and ongoing licenses expenses associated with the go-live of Project Orion).

Transactions, strategic initiatives and other costs, net consists of non-recurring or non-routine costs including costs related to severance, non-routine stock compensation expense associated with certain employee awards and professional and consulting fees for strategic projects, acquisition related costs, terminated site operations and costs related to sites held for sale or idle facilities, Project Orion, and cyber incident related costs, net of insurance recoveries.

nonop.heading: Other Income and Expense
nonop.text:
The following table presents items of other income and expense for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025.

Interest expense . Interest expense increased $4.1 million, or 10.6%, as compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025. This was primarily due to an increase in outstanding debt, most notably our 2025 Unsecured Term Loan fully drawn during December of 2025 as well as an increase in interest on the U.S. dollar denominated Revolver due to timing of draws outstanding, partially offset by a decrease in interest due to the repayment of the Private Series A Notes in January of 2026 and a decrease in interest on failed sale-leaseback facilities.

Other, net. Other, net wa s a benefit of $6.9 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to a benefit of $5.8 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The benefit during the three months ended June 30, 2026 included a $5.9 million gain from the termination of interest rate swap agreements further described in Note 5 - Derivative Financial Instruments . The benefit during the three months ended June 30, 2025 included a $2.4 million gain from the sale of the SuperFrio joint venture.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income tax expense for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $22.7 million, an increase of $19.5 million from an income tax expense of $3.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase is primarily related to changes in the blend of pre-tax book income and losses generated year over year by jurisdiction.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: For the six months ended June 30, 2026, our net cash provided by operating activities was $140.0 million, a decrease of $10.5 million compared to $150.5 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. This decrease was primarily driven by the impact of lower overall NOI which was partially offset by favorable changes in net working capital.

da.text: • Warehouse segment contribution NOI is calculated as Warehouse segment revenues less its cost of operations excluding any Depreciation and amortization, corporate-level Selling, general, and administrative expense, corporate-level Transactions, strategic initiatives and other costs, net, Impairment of long-lived assets, Net gain from sale of real estate, and all components of Other (expense) income.

sbc.text: We calculate adjusted funds from operations, or Adjusted FFO, as Core FFO adjusted for the effects of Amortization of deferred financing costs and pension withdrawal liability; Amortization of below/above market leases; Straight-line rent adjustment; Deferred income tax expense; Stock-based compensation expense; Non-real estate related depreciation and amortization; Maintenance capital expenditures; and Our share of reconciling items related to partially owned entities. We believe that Adjusted FFO is helpful to investors as a meaningful supplemental comparative performance measure of our ability to make incremental capital investments in our business and to assess our ability to fund distribution requirements from our operating activities.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: We utilize a strategic approach to capital expenditures to maintain the high quality and operational efficiency of our warehouses and equipment and ensure that our assets meet the “mission-critical” role they serve in the cold chain. The Company assesses its capital expenditure requirements regularly to support its operational infrastructure, drive strategic growth, and enhance long-term shareholder value.

Warehouse services.text: • Warehouse services contribution NOI is calculated as warehouse services revenues less labor and other service costs.

Warehouse rent and storage.text: • Warehouse rent and storage contribution NOI is calculated as warehouse rent and storage revenues less power and other facilities costs.

Transportation.heading: Transportation
Transportation.text:
Transportation services revenues are derived from fees charged for transportation of our customers products, often including fuel and capacity surcharges.

Transportation services cost of operations are primarily affected by third-party carrier costs, which are influenced by carrier factors like driver and equipment availability. In select markets, we use our drivers and assets, incurring costs like wages, fuel, tolls, insurance, and maintenance to operate these assets.

nonop.text:
The following table presents items of other income and expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.

Interest expense . Interest expense increased $8.0 million, or 23.7%, as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. This was primarily due to interest expense incurred on our 2025 Unsecured Term Loan fully drawn during December of 2025 and repaid in September 2026, as well as interest expense associated with the AUD Term Loan Facility which was fully borrowed in June 2026, increased interest expense on the U.S. dollar denominated Revolver due to timing of draws outstanding, and lower capitalized interest, partially offset by a decrease in interest due to the repayment of the Private Series A Notes in January of 2026.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income tax expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $6.5 million, an increase of $12.7 million from an income tax benefit of $6.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase is primarily impacted by the gain recognized in connection with the formation of the EQT JV. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company also recognized a discrete tax expense of $3.7 million, primarily related to a $2.8 million foreign audit settlement and $2.9 million of state tax expense related to the EQT JV formation, partially offset by a $2.0 million deferred tax benefit recognized upon the termination of a pension plan.

intro.text: Americold (NYSE: COLD) is a global leader in temperature-controlled logistics and real estate, supporting the safe, efficient movement of food worldwide. We connect producers, processors, distributors, and retailers. Leveraging deep industry expertise, advanced technology, and sustainable practices, Americold delivers reliable cold storage and transportation solutions that create lasting value for customers and communities. We operate as a self-administered and self-managed publicly traded real estate investment trust (“REIT”) with proven operating, development and acquisition expertise.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: Cash provided by investing activities consisted of $1.10 billion of proceeds from the contribution of real estate assets associated with the formation of the EQT JV, $78.1 million of total proceeds primarily related to the sale of real estate related assets, and $23.4 million of total proceeds from collection of advances to partially owned entities.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized $13.1 million of Joint venture related management fee and reimbursed costs revenues and $11.6 million of Joint venture related reimbursed costs related to the operations of the EQT JV.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized $13.1 million of Joint venture related management fee and reimbursed costs revenues and $11.6 million of Joint venture related reimbursed costs related to the operations of the EQT JV.

The Company also received $72.4 million of proceeds from the contribution of real estate assets in connection with the formation of the EQT JV that are classified as financing activities because they relate to the repurchase obligation further described in Note 13 - Investments in and Advances to Partially Owned Entities to these Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements.
This increase was primarily due to an increase in losses attributable to the Company’s ownership interest in the RSA and EQT JV joint ventures.

We also have a minority interest in two joint ventures: RSA Cold Holdings Limited (the “RSA joint venture”), which operates 2 temperature-controlled warehouses in Dubai, and Americold-EQT Cold Storage Partnership, LLC (the “EQT JV”), in which we hold a 30 % equity interest, which owns 12 temperature-controlled warehouse facilities in North America.

On August 31, 2026, the Company completed the formation of Americold-EQT Cold Storage Partnership, LLC (the “EQT JV”) with EQT Partners (“EQT”), a joint venture focused on the ownership, operation, and potential development of high-quality cold storage warehouse facilities in North America.

During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, these costs also included those associated with the formation of the EQT JV which is further described in Note 13 - Investments in and Advances to Partially Owned Entities to these Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements.
Joint venture related management fee and reimbursed costs revenues are related to management fees that the Company earns related to its property management services provided to the EQT JV.
The formation of the EQT JV is discussed further in Note 13 - Investments in and Advances to Partially Owned Entities to these Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements.
